content.text: rescue SABA for every patient; albuterol 2 puffs 4 to 6 times a day as needed is usually the drug of choice for episodic dyspnea or early exacerbation treatment.

Beta-blockers block the effect and can cause severe bronchospasm in asthma (cardioselective only, with caution, if no alternative). Loop/thiazide diuretics: hypokalemia and ECG changes can worsen. Digoxin levels may fall; consider monitoring. MAOIs/TCAs (or within 2 weeks of stopping): extreme caution, vascular effects potentiated.
Prime (4 sprays away from the face, shaking before each) before first use, after > 2 weeks unused, or if dropped. Needing more doses than usual may mean worsening asthma: seek reevaluation.

excess beta stimulation (seizures, angina, HTN or hypotension, tachycardia up to 200/min, arrhythmias, tremor, hyperglycemia, hypokalemia, metabolic acidosis); cardiac arrest and death are possible. Treat: stop the drug, symptomatic care; a cardioselective beta-blocker may be considered judiciously (it can cause bronchospasm).
